sections.title: Complex Multi-Line Analysis
sections.content: At Level 3, line graphs may contain three or more lines representing different companies or categories. Questions involve deep comparison, percentage growth rates, contribution analysis, and multi-year trends.

sections.title: Year-on-Year Growth Rate
sections.content: Year-on-Year growth means comparing each year with its previous year. For example, if revenue increases from 50000 rupees to 65000 rupees, the increase is 15000. Percentage growth is 15000 divided by 50000 multiplied by 100 which equals 30 percent.

sections.title: Cumulative and Net Change Analysis
sections.content: For total growth over multiple years, subtract the first year value from the last year value. Do not simply add percentages. Always compare actual rupee values.

sections.title: Average and Weighted Comparison
sections.content: When comparing companies, calculate total and average values separately. The company with highest average may not always have highest single year value.

sections.title: Trend Reversal and Turning Points
sections.content: If the graph shows continuous increase and then suddenly decreases, that point is called a turning point. Such questions are common in competitive exams.

sections.title: Contribution to Total
sections.content: To find contribution of a year or company, divide its value by the total and multiply by 100.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: Students often add yearly percentages instead of calculating overall percentage from initial to final value. Always use correct base value.

tricks.title: Fast Growth Comparison
tricks.explanation: Same absolute increase gives different percentage depending on base value.
tricks.example: Increase of 10000 on 20000 equals 50 percent, but on 50000 equals 20 percent.

tricks.title: Direct Net Change Trick
tricks.explanation: If overall growth is asked, subtract first year from last year directly.

tricks.title: Arithmetic Pattern Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If values increase by equal amount each year, use middle value as average.

tricks.title: Highest Contribution Trick
tricks.explanation: Divide individual value by total to find contribution percentage.

tricks.title: Combined Company Analysis
tricks.explanation: Add values of all companies year-wise for overall comparison.

tricks.title: Turning Point Identification
tricks.explanation: Find the point where increasing trend changes to decreasing trend.

tricks.title: Approximation Technique
tricks.explanation: Round numbers for faster calculation and adjust later if needed.
tricks.example: 49800 can be treated as 50000 for quick 10 percent calculation.

tricks.title: Ratio Simplification Trick
tricks.explanation: Convert large values into simplest ratio for quick comparison.

tricks.title: Percentage Difference Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Difference divided by base value multiplied by 100 gives percentage change.

tricks.title: Stepwise Analytical Method
tricks.explanation: First list yearly differences, then calculate percentages, then compare.
tricks.example: Find increase each year before calculating growth rate.
